slices.name: ws01-05-event-mode-phases

K1c: put the event-mode phase machine in the domain folder as pure code, so WS02's endpoint, WS03's hero and WS13's event-day view share one definition. domain/events/eventMode.ts exports the EventPhase type with every phase the brief names (week, dayBefore, checkin, eventDay, roundPosted, roundInProgress, between, final, after). The input is storage-free: { date, endDate, status, firstRoundTimes: per event day the first round_schedule time or null, lastRoundResultsComplete: boolean }. The Phase 0 predicates follow REDESIGN_SPEC.md WS02 exactly:
- eventEnd = (end_date ?? date) 23:59 Central
- week = 6 days before day 1 at 6:00 AM until the day before
- dayBefore = the calendar day before date
- checkin = an event day from 6:00 AM until that day's first round time
- eventDay = the rest of that day
- final = status 'completed' or lastRoundResultsComplete
- after = final until eventEnd + 48 h

Outside the window it returns null. Time arithmetic uses domain/format/centralTime.ts. The WS07 phases are declared in the type but never produced until a later input (round publications) exists; the function documents that. The endpoint GET /api/me/event-mode, src/lib/eventModeCopy.ts and the strip stay WS02 work, and WS02 calls this module instead of creating functions/utils/eventMode.ts. Add a REDESIGN_STATUS.md note so the WS02 brief is read with this path.

slices.name: ws01-07-contracts-infrastructure
slices.brief:

Registry and schemas:
- domain/contracts/registry.ts maps a route path, named as file routing names it ('tournaments/[id]', 'admin/tournaments', 'registrations/batch'), to per-method contracts { request?, query?, response }, keyed only by methods the handler file actually exports.
- Schemas live per area in domain/contracts/common.ts (ids, ISO dates, money in dollars, the { error } shape), events.ts, registration.ts and so on, with an index.ts.
- zod is imported only under domain/contracts; every other domain module stays zod-free, so domain logic the browser imports at runtime never pulls zod into the bundle. Client api types come from contracts through type-only imports (z.infer).

Server: parseBody(request, schema) goes in functions/utils/response.ts next to parseJsonBody. It returns the parsed body, or the existing errorResponse shape ({ error }) with status 400 plus a fields map. Request schemas describe what handlers accept today (optional where optional, passthrough), so nothing the current frontend sends is newly rejected. Responses are not validated at runtime in production; contract tests validate them.

Harness: expectContract(result, schema) in test/integration/harness.ts parses result.json() strictly and prints the zod issues.

Ratchet: extract collectRoutes from route-audit.test.ts into test/unit/routes.ts. test/unit/contract-coverage.test.ts lists every handler file under functions/api plus the page routes functions/tournaments/[id].ts and functions/clubs/[id].ts, with their exported onRequest methods. Each method needs a registry entry, a line in test/unit/contracts-pending.ts, or (for the two page routes, which serve HTML with link-preview meta and are covered by test/integration/preview.test.ts) a line in its EXCLUDED list with a reason. The test fails when a route is in two lists, or when a registry entry names a method the file does not export. The pending list's length is pinned in the file, so it can only shrink.

Prove the pattern on GET /api/tournaments with test/integration/contracts/tournaments-list.test.ts. Each later slice that touches an endpoint writes its contract and contract test and removes it from the pending list.

sequencing_rationale:
K's structural decisions come first and the design tokens last. Each risky change sits in its own slice, and the work merges from the one branch (redesign/ws01-design-system) in four checkpoints.

Part 1 (slices 1 to 8, checkpoint A) changes nothing at runtime:
- the preview database with its guard, first, so the branch is never pushed without its own binding (a branch pushed earlier would get a Pages preview bound to production lca-db)
- the flags, the status map and the jsdom test setup
- the domain folder with its format helpers, the moved mirror rules and the event-mode phases
- the Drizzle baseline, with the depth-aware splitSql and a safety test that reads drizzle-kit's real output
- the contract ratchet (K answers the contracts question before slice 7)
- an additive migration that creates and backfills the sections and schedules tables

Drizzle comes before the migration so that 0052 is generated, the drift test covers it, and the safety test reads Drizzle's quoted names, ON UPDATE clauses and ADD without COLUMN before any Drizzle SQL lands. migrate-db.yml applies migrations to production on every merge to main, so 0053's triggers, including an AFTER UPDATE trigger on tournaments, keep the tables in step with every write the old code makes for the whole soak. Tier prices are never stored as copies of tournament columns, so edits to deadlines and fees need no sync. Checkpoint A does not merge until K has pasted the preview id, and K migrates lca-db-preview from the branch before reviewing each checkpoint's preview.

Part 2 (slices 9 to 15, checkpoint B) makes the data change dual-path:
- the single writer first, writing table rows and then the JSON mirror in today's shape, in one Drizzle batch
- the readers in four small groups: player registration, admin entry, server display, client
- then schedules, then the pricing decision

At every point the JSON column is a complete mirror, so any reader commit can be reverted alone. The writer, reader and schedule audit tests prove when no JSON reader or raw tournaments response is left. Prices come from the section row plus the live tournament columns, so existing pricing tests stay green. The member-discount retirement and requires_lca_membership get their own slice, because the server price change cannot sit behind a frontend flag and waits for K's production query.

Part 3 (slices 16 to 19, checkpoint C) does the folder moves by script with renames-only commits:
- server helpers
- client lib (the domain shims stay in src/lib)
- the api.ts split behind a barrel
- components plus boundary lint

The moves come after the data work so they do not rebase over semantic edits, and before the codemods and component work so those land on final paths. Each move is checked by the gate, the Pages Functions build, the worker dry-run and verify-move.

Part 4 (slices 20 to 32, checkpoint D) is the design system:
- the Playwright harness first, because every later design slice adds browser checks and compares against its flag-off baseline; it also carries the planned family-registration and publish-round e2e specs
- then tokens, scope mechanism, the two semantic colour codemods, gold-ink, components, chess data, brand marks, hero and images, heritage fonts, heritage layout
- the AC1 sweep last, because it tests everything before it

Drizzle conversion of old queries uses a narrow meaning of 'touched': a query converts when a slice changes its SQL text or bound values. Queries whose rows are only post-processed differently stay as raw D1. When a converted statement shares a batch, the whole batch moves to Drizzle's db.batch.

Sections and schedules become tables: tournament_sections with fee_regular (null inherits the tournament entry fee), optional explicit fee_early and fee_late, and a cap; tournament_schedules with merge_round and is_primary; tournament_schedule_rounds; and registrations.section_id and schedule_id. These replace DESIGN_REPLAN_phase1 8.1's schedules JSON column, tournaments.merge_round and the cap key in the JSON.
